instruction:
Fix `packages/excalidraw/tests/selection.test.tsx` for these problems, changing only what they need, following the conventions in the shared brief:
1. Round 2. Still failing in describe("lasso selection mode") after round 1 (yarn test:app --watch=false packages/excalidraw/tests/selection.test.tsx): (1) "selects a group in contain mode only when all group members are enclosed": AssertionError: expected +0 to be 2 at selection.test.tsx:1558 (the second lasso). (2) "frame child extending past the frame edge > contain mode: enclosing the visible part selects the child, not the frame": expected +0 to be 1 at :1615. (3) "frame child extending past the frame edge > overlap mode: touching the clipped-out part selects the child": expected +0 to be 1 at :1639. All other tests in the suite pass, including the overlap group test and the frame tests expecting [] or [frame.id]. Diagnosis for (1): the first lasso ends with mouse.up() at (-20,-20) and the second lasso's mouse.downAt is at the same (-20,-20) right after, which the editor treats as a double-click instead of a new lasso. Start the second lasso at a different empty-canvas point (e.g. rectLasso(-25, -25, 170, 70)), or reset the pointer/clock between lassos the way other tests in this file do. Diagnosis for (2) and (3): the child is never selected through the pointer path even in unchanged overlap mode, while the direct-call equivalents in packages/excalidraw/tests/lasso.test.tsx pass. Build the frame scene the way the existing pointer-driven frame-child box-selection tests in this file do (the suite near lines 734-787: how the frame and child are created and put into the scene, element order, and any act()/render step before the pointer gesture), and start each lasso on empty canvas outside both the frame and the child. Keep every expectation as stated: contain visible-part lasso selects [child.id] only; overlap hidden-part lasso (x 110..160) selects [child.id]; do not change any other test.

The file's current text is under Inputs, marked "current text"; your edits apply to exactly that text.

## Answer
Return ONLY a JSON object {"path": "packages/excalidraw/tests/selection.test.tsx", "edits": [{"search": "<text copied exactly from the current text>", "replace": "<its replacement>"}]} with no other text. Each search must appear exactly once in the current text; the edits apply in order.
If the file does not exist yet, or the change rewrites most of it, return {"path": "packages/excalidraw/tests/selection.test.tsx", "content": "<the complete file>"} instead.
